meta.title.data-collection: Data Collection: gathering a client's documents, from 0 to 100% | Case study by Hugo Ferrer
meta.desc.data-collection: Case study: discovery and design of document collection for an HR and finance consulting firm. Eight interviews, four journeys, and one principle: see what is missing the moment a file arrives.

dc.hook.quote: “You go back and forth 12 times and the client still never sends you the right month.”
dc.s1.title: The problem: four sticking points, always the same
dc.s1.intro: Every engagement at the firm starts with the same step: getting the client's documents, sometimes covering three years and hundreds of sites. This collection ran on emails, a file-sharing space and spreadsheets.
dc.s1.k1.d: Endless back-and-forth with the client, and no signal when a file is uploaded.
dc.s1.k1.q: “A few days go by between the moment they upload the docs and the moment we notice.”
dc.s1.k2.d: No way to know whether a case file is complete without opening the files one by one.
dc.s1.k2.q: “Sometimes the thing is called 2025, you open it, and it's 2024.”
dc.s1.k3.d: Converting, cleaning and normalising payroll data can take several days per case.
dc.s1.k3.q: “It can happen that we hit refresh and wait three hours.”
dc.s1.k4.d: Each new year, the same collection starts again for ongoing cases and ties up the teams for months.
dc.s2.title: The approach: listen first, design second
dc.s2.intro: Eight interviews across four areas of expertise, with consultants, payroll experts, managers, an operations lead and a business developer. Each interview was recorded and transcribed, then completed by watching real case files on screen. The area most advanced on the subject served as the pilot.
dc.s2.st1.d: Eight recorded interviews, and real case files opened on screen.
dc.s2.st2.d: Every step of the collection, from signature to report.
dc.s2.st3.d: One main persona: the consultant who runs the collection.
dc.s2.st4.d: Each difficulty tied to a possible solution.
dc.s2.f.title: What the interviews established
dc.s2.f.legend: Frequency observed across the five interviews of the pilot area.
dc.s2.f1: Collection is a game of ping-pong, with no signal when a file arrives.
dc.s2.f2: Reprocessing the data is the biggest time sink: every payroll software has its own layout.
dc.s2.f3: An incomplete case file does not show on arrival: it is discovered in the middle of the analysis.
dc.s2.f4: The DSN, the payroll return French employers file every month, is the only standardised data: the one everyone trusts.
dc.s2.f5: The tool should raise alerts, never decide in the consultant's place.
dc.s2.quote: “We stop digging, and we lose the expertise.”
dc.s2.cite: A senior consultant, about a fully automated audit
dc.s3.title: The system: six decisions drawn from the interviews
dc.s3.intro: Each decision answers a finding and, most of the time, says what it rules out. Screens are shown as excerpts, with fictional data.
dc.s3.loop.title: Four journeys, a single loop
dc.s3.loop.legend: One case file passes from hand to hand: each role has its own journey.
dc.s3.loop1.d: Create the client, prepare and send the initial request.
dc.s3.loop2.d: Receive the request, upload, fix or sort the files.
dc.s3.loop3.d: Find the client to assign, apply, then save.
dc.s3.loop4.d: Review the files, upload on the client's behalf and prepare a reminder.
dc.s3.loop5.d: Receive a reminder, and requests for further documents.
dc.d1.t: See what is missing the moment a file arrives
dc.d1.d: Every upload is checked on arrival: right format, right period, missing months. A view by site and by month shows the gaps at a glance.
dc.d1.out: Opening the files one by one to check.
dc.d1.q: “Green, I have the DSN. Red, I don't.”
dc.shot.aria: Mockup excerpt, scrollable sideways on small screens
dc.d1.alt: Mockup excerpt, interface in French: the “What is still missing” card lists three document types to complete, next to the upload area.
dc.d1.n1: The list of what is missing, updated with every upload.
dc.d1.n2: The file is checked on arrival: format, period, site.
dc.shot.caption: Mockup excerpt, fictional data, interface in French.
dc.d2.d: No status to fill in by hand: every state of the case file follows from a real action.
dc.d2.out: A tracking tool that has to be filled in. The previous one had been abandoned, too slow to keep up to date.
dc.d3.d: A core set of documents without which no case can start, and a standard collection pack.
dc.d3.out: The exhaustive questionnaire sent to the client.
dc.d4.t: Client side: a list and a guided upload
dc.d4.d: The client needs a clear instruction, not a project management tool. The file itself says where it belongs: the site and the month are read at every upload.
dc.d4.out: The full portal with a dashboard.
dc.d5.t: The tool alerts, the consultant decides
dc.d5.d: A rejected file shows its reason in plain words and the action expected. The analysis itself stays in the experts' hands.
dc.d5.out: The fully automated audit, a black box that would smooth over the anomalies only they know how to spot.
dc.d5.alt: Mockup excerpt, interface in French: the DSN upload area, then five rejected files, each with its reason and a button to upload it again.
dc.d5.n1: Nothing to fill in: the site number (SIRET) and the month are read from each file.
dc.d5.n2: Each rejection gives its reason and the action expected.
dc.d6.d: The reminder only covers documents still expected: complete items are not requested again. Automatic reminders stop for each complete, validated set.
dc.d6.alt: Excerpt from the reminder dialog, interface in French: only the three documents still to be provided are ticked.
dc.d6.caption: The reminder dialog: only the documents still to be provided are ticked.

dc.s4.aud.title: An audit before acceptance testing
dc.s4.aud.d: I reread the four journeys as a single story and listed the inconsistencies: copy that does not match the state on screen, reference figures that differ from one screen to the next, duplicate naming, gaps in the journey.
dc.s4.aud.cases: Eight edge cases to replay in the prototype
dc.s4.num.title: What about the numbers?
dc.s4.num.d: There are no post-launch figures yet, and I will not make any up. Discovery showed that collection time was not measured anywhere: the design therefore timestamps each step (request, upload, complete case file), to have a baseline for comparison.
dc.s4.hand.title: The handoff
dc.s4.hand.d: The development team praised the journeys for their precision and technical clarity.
dc.s4.learn.title: What I take away
dc.s4.l1: A payslip cannot be read like a generic document: every payroll software has its own layout, so each one needs its own template.
dc.s4.l2: A tracking tool that asks people to enter statuses by hand ends up abandoned.
dc.s4.l3: The client does not want to follow a project online: they want a clear upload instruction.
dc.s4.l4: Automation should surface alerts and leave the investigation to the experts.
dc.end.title: A business tool to make readable?
dc.end.sub: Let's talk about your product: 30 minutes to understand your context.
dc.end.note: Reply within 48h. Open to embedded support or focused missions.
